notes: Full description: DeviationStore::active_at (pkix-lint/src/deviation.rs:454), active_for_lint (line 461), and expired_at (line 474) all return impl Iterator but are not annotated with #[must_use]. Calling these methods without consuming the returned iterator is a silent no-op — the compiler emits no warning. This is particularly dangerous for expired_at, which is described as 'used by corpus-reporting tools to surface deviations that need renewal': if a caller writes 'store.expired_at(now);' thinking it performs a side effect, the bug is invisible. Fix: add #[must_use] to all three methods. This is consistent with Rust stdlib Iterator-returning methods (e.g., slice::iter(), HashMap::values()) which have #[must_use] or inherit it from the Iterator type. Also affected: DeviationStore::all() (line 449) lacks #[must_use] but returns a slice reference, which is also silently discardable.
title: RUSTY: DeviationStore iterator methods missing #[must_use]
